Preconditions: Store locator page loaded; "Search Nearby" tab active
Test Steps: Enter a locality/city known to have outlets in #OutletSearch, click Search
Expected Result: Page navigates with ?search=<term> in the URL; matching outlets render in the list and on the map
Remarks: Verified live: search=Delhi returned 0 outlets (no Nayara pumps in Delhi test data) — navigation and rendering confirmed, not the outlet count

Test Steps: Start typing a real place name into #OutletSearch
Expected Result: A Google Places .pac-item suggestion dropdown appears within a few seconds
Remarks: Exercised internally while driving the route-search cases; can flake if the Maps API key is rate/quota-limited

Test Steps: Type a partial place name, then press ArrowDown then Enter (or click) a suggestion
Expected Result: Input value updates to the selected place; form remains submittable

Test Steps: Clear #OutletSearch, attempt to submit the form
Expected Result: Native HTML5 required validation blocks submission; no page navigation occurs

Test Steps: Enter a nonsense string with no matching outlets (e.g. zzqxnonexistentplace9999), submit
Expected Result: Page loads normally (no 500 / blank page); shows zero results or an appropriate fallback, not a crash

Test Steps: Enter a script/markup-injection payload (e.g. <script>alert(1)</script>), submit
Expected Result: No script executes, no JS alert/dialog fires, and the payload is not rendered unescaped in the resulting page

Test Steps: Enter a known locality with leading/trailing spaces (e.g. "  Faridabad  "), submit
Expected Result: Same result set as the trimmed term; no validation error is raised for the whitespace

Test Steps: Run the same search once in all caps ("FARIDABAD") and once in lower case ("faridabad")
Expected Result: Both searches return an identical result set

Test Steps: Focus #OutletSearch, type a valid term, press Enter instead of clicking the Search button
Expected Result: Form submits and behaves identically to clicking the Search button

Preconditions: A valid search has been run and returned results
Test Steps: Compare the number of entries in the outlet list against the number of pins on the map
Expected Result: List entry count equals map marker count
Remarks: Needs map-canvas inspection, not just DOM text — outside what the current script asserts

Test Steps: Open the storelocator URL directly with a query string, e.g. .../storelocator/<id>?search=<term>
Expected Result: Page loads already filtered to that term without requiring a manual re-submit

Test Steps: Paste a very long string (500+ characters) into #OutletSearch, submit
Expected Result: Graceful no-match handling; no layout break, no server error

Test Steps: Open the Advanced Search tab and inspect the #OutletState dropdown
Expected Result: State dropdown lists all expected states/regions (25 confirmed on the verified UAT instance)

Preconditions: "Advanced Search" tab active, no State selected
Test Steps: Select any non-blank State option
Expected Result: #OutletCity dropdown's options change (via AJAX) from the default "All"-only list

Preconditions: Page freshly loaded, State not yet touched
Test Steps: Inspect #OutletCity without selecting a State
Expected Result: City shows a disabled/placeholder state, e.g. "Please select state first"
Remarks: Placeholder text confirmed present in page markup (jsCityDisableStatus); presence is not asserted by the automated script

Preconditions: A State has been selected (see TC-ADV-02)
Test Steps: Select a specific City from the repopulated #OutletCity dropdown
Expected Result: #OutletLocality dropdown updates to that city's localities

Preconditions: A State has been selected; City/Locality left as "All"
Test Steps: Submit the Advanced Search form
Expected Result: Page navigates to a state-scoped URL/title; outlets shown belong to the selected state (verified: selecting Andhra Pradesh returned genuinely different, correctly-addressed Ananthapur-area outlets, not the default Haryana set)
Remarks: Cross-checking that every returned outlet's address actually matches the selected state is currently a manual step

Test Steps: Reset/leave #OutletState blank, attempt to submit
Expected Result: Native HTML5 required validation blocks submission

Preconditions: State A and a specific City X are selected
Test Steps: Change the State dropdown to a different State B
Expected Result: City/Locality reset to "All"/disabled rather than silently retaining State A's City X

Preconditions: A State/City/Locality combination with zero matching outlets is known/available
Test Steps: Select that combination and submit
Expected Result: A clear "no stores found" message renders — not a blank or broken page

Preconditions: A State search returning more than one page of outlets has been submitted
Test Steps: Click page 2, 3, Next, and Last controls in turn
Expected Result: Each control loads a different, correct subset of outlets for the same filtered search

Preconditions: A State/City/Locality search has been submitted
Test Steps: Click the browser Back button
Expected Result: Previously selected State/City/Locality values are restored on the form, not reset to defaults

Test Steps: Enter identical text into #OutletSourceAddress and #OutletDestinationAddress, submit
Expected Result: Inline error "Source and destination cannot be the same" becomes visible; the form does not navigate away

Test Steps: Fill one of source/destination, leave the other empty, attempt to submit
Expected Result: Native HTML5 required validation blocks submission

Test Steps: Pick distinct autocomplete suggestions for source and destination, submit
Expected Result: Page navigates; outlets along/near the route render, and the map shows a route polyline
Remarks: Script records this as SKIP (not FAIL) if no live autocomplete suggestion appears within ~6s — that reflects Google Places API availability/quota, not the site's own search logic

Test Steps: Enter a nonsense string as source or destination, submit
Expected Result: Graceful "location not found" handling; no crash

Test Steps: Submit source=A/destination=B, then submit source=B/destination=A
Expected Result: Both directions return valid (possibly different) results; neither errors

Test Steps: Enter a source and destination that are far apart (e.g. different states)
Expected Result: Nearest matches return within a reasonable time; no timeout

Test Steps: Type into the source field, then type into the destination field
Expected Result: Each field's autocomplete suggestion list reflects only its own current input, not the other field's

Preconditions: All three search tabs present on the page
Test Steps: Click each search-type tab in turn
Expected Result: Exactly the clicked tab's form becomes visible; the other panels hide

Preconditions: At least two search types present
Test Steps: Run a search under type A, then switch to type B and run a search
Expected Result: Type B's submission uses only its own form fields' values, with no leftover query params from type A

Test Steps: Exercise every available search type on the page
Expected Result: No uncaught JS pageerror events fire in the browser console

Preconditions: Locality and/or Route search present (both depend on Google Places)
Test Steps: Exercise autocomplete-driven searches (typing into #OutletSearch / source / destination fields)
Expected Result: No "rate-limit exceeded" / OVER_QUERY_LIMIT / RequestDenied messages appear in the console
Remarks: Real observed failure mode on the UAT Maps key at time of writing — see Known Issues in the test-case doc

Preconditions: A search has been run and results are shown
Test Steps: Reload the page without changing the URL
Expected Result: The same query params reproduce the same filtered result set after reload

Preconditions: Results are showing from any search type
Test Steps: Click Call, Map, and Website on a result entry
Expected Result: Each action opens/behaves correctly for the specific outlet it's attached to

Test Steps: Repeat the key scenarios above (tab switch, one search per type) at mobile width
Expected Result: Tabs, inputs, and buttons remain usable; no overlap or clipping
Remarks: The accessibility auditor in this repo (npm run audit) already flags target-size and focus issues generically — don't duplicate that logic here, just re-run it against search-result pages

Test Steps: Time each search type from submit click to results rendering
Expected Result: No unbounded loading spinner; completes within a few seconds under normal load

Test Steps: Throttle the network (e.g. DevTools "Slow 3G") and submit a search mid-load
Expected Result: No silent failure — either the native form GET still completes or a clear loading/error state is shown
